section_summary: This section documents Japanese exchange controls and their effects on American firms’ funds, dividends, royalties, imports, and shipping revenues. It includes consular reports on Japanese finance and North China currency policy, correspondence about blocked company funds, and a sustained appeal by American President Lines for help remitting its yen revenues. The final two pages begin a second copy of that appeal, which continues beyond this section.

subfiles.title: Report on American firms and Japanese exchange controls, concluding sections
subfiles.about: The report assesses blocked American funds, Japanese exchange policy, and prospects for remitting profits.
subfiles.summary: The closing sections describe blocked film proceeds, Singer Sewing Machine Company's growing yen holdings and liquidation of its Japanese business, and Japanese restrictions on imports and currency transfers. The report attributes the pressure on Japan's reserves chiefly to falling exports, while warning that delayed exchange contracts defer payment for earlier imports. It finds poor prospects for remitting profits, dividends, and royalties and ends with a confidential list of company sources.

subfiles.title: Tsingtao export embargo and tobacco currency requirements
subfiles.about: Japanese authorities condition tobacco exports on use of Federal Reserve Bank currency.
subfiles.summary: The Yee Tsung Tobacco Company secured a limited lifting of the embargo for shipments to northern ports. Japanese authorities continued to require Federal Reserve Bank currency for exports to Shanghai and sought greater control of North China's tobacco trade.

subfiles.title: Rieser Company telegram on Chefoo shipment embargo
subfiles.about: The company seeks redress for an embargo on goods already paid for in Chinese currency.
subfiles.summary: Rieser asks for help after Japanese officials require settlement through the Yokohama Specie Bank.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Rieser Company correspondence
subfiles.about: The division decides that Rieser's January 25 letter requires no separate reply.
subfiles.summary: The Department's earlier letter had substantially addressed Rieser's points.

subfiles.title: Rieser Company request for extension of shipment relief
subfiles.about: Rieser asks the Department to seek another extension of relief from the Japanese embargo.
subfiles.summary: The company wants to use its remaining Chinese currency and cites exchange disadvantages against Swatow competitors.

subfiles.title: Rieser Company acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Rieser acknowledges Hamilton's letter about Americans operating in China.
subfiles.summary: The company thanks the Department for its efforts.

subfiles.title: Charge-out form for Tsingtao telegram
subfiles.about: A later records form tracks a Tsingtao telegram in file 894.5151.
subfiles.summary: The form records file, telegram, and charge-out details.

subfiles.title: File note for Osaka exchange-control despatch
subfiles.about: The note points to Makinson's report on Finance Minister Ikeda's Osaka remarks.
subfiles.summary: It cross-references file 894.51/608.

subfiles.title: Visit to Osaka of Minister of Finance and Governor of the Bank of Japan
subfiles.from: George M. Makinson, American Consul General, Osaka
subfiles.about: Makinson reports speeches and discussions on Japanese finance, controls, and regional economic policy.
subfiles.summary: Ikeda disclosed figures on gold shipments and discussed debt, bonds, budgets, prices, trade, and state control; Yuki emphasized savings and defended the note issue. Osaka industrial and commercial leaders questioned how controls were designed and administered, sought tax and credit changes, and debated the economic roles of Manchuria and China. Makinson records press reactions and concern about fuller use of the National Mobilization Act.

subfiles.title: American Cotton Cooperative Association blocked funds
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports approval of remittance applications connected with imported raw cotton.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office says all related applications to remit settlement funds have been approved.

subfiles.title: Bates International Bag Company blocked funds
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports partial permission to remit funds owed under a patent licence.
subfiles.summary: The Oriental Paper Bag Company received permission to remit 9,607; the balance remained under consideration.

subfiles.title: Status of five companies' blocked funds
subfiles.about: The division summarizes Embassy efforts to release funds for five American companies.
subfiles.summary: Japanese permits reportedly cover all Ford Motor and American Cotton Cooperative Association funds, most Orvis Brothers and International Telephone and Telegraph funds, and part of Bates International Bag Company's funds. Some balances or outcomes remain uncertain.

subfiles.title: Orvis Brothers blocked funds
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports a permitted export-bill arrangement for money owed to Orvis Brothers.
subfiles.summary: The arrangement covered cotton goods intended to realize 380,000 yen, but reported proceeds still left an apparent balance. The Embassy had not learned whether Orvis Brothers was satisfied.

subfiles.title: Ford Motor Company blocked dividends
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports permission to remit Ford Motor Company's blocked dividends.
subfiles.summary: Following Ford's appeal and informal Embassy contact, the Foreign Office reported approval of the 2,253,985.93-yen remittance.

subfiles.title: Maritime Commission referral of American President Lines complaint
subfiles.from: E. S. Land, United States Maritime Commission
subfiles.about: Land forwards a shipping company's complaint about withdrawing yen from Japan.
subfiles.summary: He asks the Department to assist American President Lines.

subfiles.title: American President Lines complaint to Admiral Land
subfiles.from: Joseph R. Sheehan, American President Lines
subfiles.about: Sheehan describes mounting yen balances and asks whether State Department intervention could help.
subfiles.summary: The company held roughly 620,000 yen as Japanese permits slowed and spread dollar conversion across later months. Sheehan describes changes to ticket and freight practices intended to limit further yen accumulation.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on steamship companies' blocked revenues
subfiles.about: A departmental officer argues for action on American President Lines' blocked revenues.
subfiles.summary: The officer cites competitive harm and a successful intervention involving United States Lines in Germany.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Embassy on American President Lines
subfiles.about: The Department directs the Embassy to seek reciprocal treatment for American shipping remittances.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is to investigate the company's blocked yen and press Japanese authorities, noting that Japanese lines may freely remit their United States balances.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Joseph R. Sheehan
subfiles.about: Hamilton tells Sheehan that the Embassy has been instructed to raise the blocked-revenue issue.
subfiles.summary: The letter acknowledges Sheehan's complaint and reports the Department's instruction.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Admiral Land
subfiles.about: Sayre reports the Embassy instruction concerning American President Lines.
subfiles.summary: The Department has also informed the company of its action.

subfiles.title: American President Lines appeal concerning blocked yen
subfiles.from: W. G. McAdoo, American President Lines
subfiles.about: McAdoo seeks vigorous intervention over delayed conversion of the company's Japanese yen revenues.
subfiles.summary: McAdoo traces increasingly restrictive Japanese permits and reports about 720,732 yen blocked as of July 7. He argues that delay and possible yen depreciation threaten the company's finances and that it receives worse treatment than Japanese and at least one other foreign line. He rejects most Japanese complaints about its practices, explains why crews receive dollar advances, and asks for prompt monthly remittance permits.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at July 7, 1939
subfiles.about: The attached schedule tabulates monthly yen receipts, conversions, permits, and unpermitted balances.
subfiles.summary: Two views of Schedule A show 658,776.36 yen without permits.

subfiles.title: Instructions on crew advances in Japanese and Italian ports
subfiles.from: Arthur B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.about: The company limits when crews may receive dollar advances before port calls.
subfiles.summary: Dollar advances for Yokohama, Kobe, and Naples require a call within one day.

subfiles.title: Dodge and Seymour profits in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Japanese pressure on Dodge and Seymour to transfer profits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The profits arose from American manufacturers' goods used in munitions production.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Dodge and Seymour
subfiles.about: The division considers the Embassy's Dodge and Seymour telegram.
subfiles.summary: It recommends awaiting a direct approach from the company.

subfiles.title: Embassy representations for American President Lines
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew reports oral representations to speed the company's pending and future remittances.
subfiles.summary: About 390,000 yen awaited remittance, partly covered by permits through June.

subfiles.title: Department update to Joseph R. Sheehan
subfiles.about: Hamilton relays the Embassy's report on permits and representations.
subfiles.summary: He reports approximately 390,000 yen awaiting remittance.

subfiles.title: Department update to Admiral Land
subfiles.about: Messersmith reports the Embassy's representations on American President Lines' yen.
subfiles.summary: Permits partly covered the approximately 390,000 yen then reported as awaiting remittance.

subfiles.title: Sheehan acknowledgment of Department action
subfiles.about: Sheehan acknowledges the Department's April 8 letter.
subfiles.summary: He thanks the Department for its prompt action.

subfiles.title: Correction of American President Lines yen balance
subfiles.about: Sheehan explains the difference between two reported yen balances.
subfiles.summary: The 390,000-yen figure applied at February's end; holdings had since risen to about 725,000 yen.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese gold and foreign exchange resources
subfiles.about: The note cross-references Luthringer's study of Japan's external resources.
subfiles.summary: It points to a memorandum in file 894.51/632.

subfiles.title: Forwarded report on North China currency and export controls
subfiles.about: A forwarded report describes prospective controls intended to strengthen Federal Reserve currency.
subfiles.summary: It says restrictions on Japanese imports into North China may ease while export and exchange controls expand to all commodities.

subfiles.title: Tokyo report on North China currency and export controls
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports proposed trade measures to support Federal Reserve currency.
subfiles.summary: After Hidaka's inspection trip, authorities reportedly planned more Japanese imports and wider export controls in North China. A banker expected reduced pressure on the currency.

subfiles.title: Permits for American President Lines' earlier funds
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports permits for funds held through March 31.
subfiles.summary: Remittances must occur in installments from May through August; the Embassy will press for later funds.

subfiles.title: Further instruction on regular shipping remittances
subfiles.about: The Department directs renewed representations for regular transfer of American President Lines revenues.
subfiles.summary: It asks Japan to provide reciprocal, effective arrangements for continuously accruing yen.

subfiles.title: Charge-out form for Tokyo telegram
subfiles.about: A later records form tracks Tokyo telegram 287 in file 894.5151/138.
subfiles.summary: The form records telegram and charge-out details.

subfiles.title: Handwritten note on shipping-remittance precedents
subfiles.about: The writer discusses precedents for unobstructed remittance of shipping revenues.
subfiles.summary: Colleagues recall only the German case as a precedent.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on McAdoo's American President Lines appeal
subfiles.about: The division assesses the company's July 12 appeal and proposes stronger representations.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reviews blocked funds, financial risk, alleged discrimination, and Japan's complaints about company practices. It recommends emphasizing the need for a reliable remittance system and refers to an attached draft telegram.

subfiles.title: American President Lines appeal concerning blocked yen, second copy
subfiles.from: W. G. McAdoo, American President Lines
subfiles.about: A second copy begins McAdoo's appeal for intervention over blocked yen revenues.
subfiles.summary: These pages repeat the letter's opening and its account of tightening exchange permits; the copy continues after page 400.
